::: about-intro
<p class="about-section-label">MY PERSPECTIVE</p>

## Models matter. So do their limits.

Models help organise our thinking, but they do not remove uncertainty. The assumptions we make, the incentives people face, the institutions surrounding a problem and the limits of the available data all shape what a model can tell us.

The tension between useful abstraction and messy reality connects much of my writing.
:::

::: about-grid
::: about-panel
<span>01</span>

### Background

My academic background is in economics and business analytics. I want to work in economics, and in time I hope to pursue deeper study in statistics as well.
:::

::: about-panel
<span>02</span>

### What I write about

The subjects range from economics and public policy to geopolitics, applied statistics and theology. Some pieces are analytical; others begin with a question I want to follow further.
:::

::: about-panel
<span>03</span>

### Why I write

This blog is where I work through ideas in public: testing an argument, examining a policy or trying to understand why a neat model breaks down in practice.
:::
